records.source: לֹֽא־תִרְאֶה֩ אֶת־שׁ֨וֹר אָחִ֜יךָ א֤וֹ אֶת־שֵׂיוֹ֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֵ֖ם לְאָחִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: Not you shall see [the] ox of your brother or his sheep straying and hide yourself from them; surely you shall bring them back to your brother.
pieces: If you see a fellow Israelite's ox or sheep wandering loose, do not look the other way. Be sure to take the animal back to him.

L.1: You shall not see your brother's ox or his sheep straying and hide yourself from them; you shall surely bring them back to your brother.

R.1: You may see that a fellow Israelite's ox or sheep has wandered off. Do not just ignore it. Take it back to its owner.

decisions.choice: hide yourself from them: look away, act as if you had not seen
decisions.reason: The verb means to hide or conceal oneself. Here it is turning a blind eye: seeing a neighbor's loss and choosing not to get involved. The same word returns in verses 3 and 4, and Isaiah 58:7 uses it for refusing to help one's own people in need.

decisions.choice: your brother: a fellow Israelite, not only a blood brother
decisions.reason: In Deuteronomy's laws "brother" is any member of the people of Israel (15:2-3, 7, 12). The rule in Exodus 23:4 goes further and requires the same care for the stray ox or donkey of an enemy.

decisions.choice: still Moses speaking: part of the speech that began at 5:1
decisions.reason: The chapter lies inside Moses' long speech of 5:1-26:19, so no new speech begins here. Verses 1-12 are a run of short laws on everyday life: lost animals and goods, clothing, birds' nests, roofs, mixed seed, plowing, cloth and tassels.

decisions.choice: a fellow Israelite / its owner
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "your brother". Balanced and Readable say "fellow Israelite", the person meant (see the meaning decision), as in 15:2-3. Readable says "its owner" for the second "your brother", which is the point of the rule.

decisions.choice: look the other way / just ignore it
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the Hebrew "hide yourself" with everyday expressions. Literal keeps the picture.

records.heading: Your neighbor’s animals

records.source: וְאִם־לֹ֨א קָר֥וֹב אָחִ֛יךָ אֵלֶ֖יךָ וְלֹ֣א יְדַעְתּ֑וֹ וַאֲסַפְתּוֹ֙ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ בֵּיתֶ֔ךָ וְהָיָ֣ה עִמְּךָ֗ עַ֣ד דְּרֹ֤שׁ אָחִ֨יךָ֙ אֹת֔וֹ וַהֲשֵׁבֹת֖וֹ לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And if not near [is] your brother to you and not you know him, then you shall gather it into [the] midst of your house, and it shall be with you until seeks your brother it, and you shall return it to him.
pieces: If the owner does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, take the animal home with you and keep it until he comes looking for it. Then give it back to him.

L.2: And if your brother is not near to you, or you do not know him, then you shall gather it into your house, and it shall be with you until your brother seeks it; then you shall return it to him.

R.2: The owner may live far away, or you may not know who the owner is. Then take the animal home and keep it until the owner comes looking for it. Then give it back.

decisions.choice: you do not know him: you do not know who the owner is
decisions.reason: The two cases are a distance too great to walk the animal back, and not knowing whose it is. Either way the finder may not keep it or leave it.

decisions.choice: gather it into your house: take it into your own care until it is claimed
decisions.reason: Animals were often kept in the courtyard or the lower part of the house. The finder is to look after the animal, feeding it, until the owner comes to ask about it, so that nothing is lost to him.

decisions.choice: seeks it: comes looking for it, asks after it
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or inquire. The owner's search is the signal for the finder to hand it back.

decisions.choice: the owner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the owner" for "your brother" in this verse, since the point is whose the animal is; verse 1 has already said he is a fellow Israelite.

records.source: וְכֵ֧ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה לַחֲמֹר֗וֹ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂה֮ לְשִׂמְלָתוֹ֒ וְכֵ֣ן תַּעֲשֶׂ֜ה לְכָל־אֲבֵדַ֥ת אָחִ֛יךָ אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאבַ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נּוּ וּמְצָאתָ֑הּ לֹ֥א תוּכַ֖ל לְהִתְעַלֵּֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And thus you shall do for his donkey, and thus you shall do for his garment, and thus you shall do for every lost thing of your brother which is lost from him and you find it; not you are able to hide yourself.
pieces: Do the same with a donkey or a cloak, or anything else a fellow Israelite loses and you find. You must not look the other way.

L.3: And so you shall do with his donkey, and so you shall do with his garment, and so you shall do with every lost thing of your brother's that he loses and you find; you may not hide yourself.

R.3: Do the same if you find a fellow Israelite's donkey or coat, or anything else that person has lost. Do not act as if you did not see it.

decisions.choice: his garment: the outer cloak
decisions.reason: The word is the large outer garment, which a poor man also slept in at night (Exodus 22:25-26). It stands here as an example of a valuable thing that might be dropped and found.

decisions.choice: you are not able to hide yourself: you are not permitted to ignore it
decisions.reason: "You are not able" here means "you may not": it is a prohibition, not a statement of what is possible. The same use comes in verses 19 and 29.

decisions.choice: cloak / coat
decisions.reason: Balanced says "cloak", Readable "coat", for the outer garment named here; Literal keeps the general word "garment".

records.source: לֹא־תִרְאֶה֩ אֶת־חֲמ֨וֹר אָחִ֜יךָ א֤וֹ שׁוֹרוֹ֙ נֹפְלִ֣ים בַּדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם הָקֵ֥ם תָּקִ֖ים עִמּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: Not you shall see [the] donkey of your brother or his ox fallen on the road and hide yourself from them; surely you shall raise [them] up with him.
pieces: If you see a fellow Israelite's donkey or ox fallen on the road, do not look the other way. Be sure to help him get it back on its feet.

L.4: You shall not see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road and hide yourself from them; you shall surely raise [them] up with him.

R.4: You may see that a fellow Israelite's donkey or ox has fallen down on the road. Do not ignore it. Help the owner get the animal up again.

decisions.choice: a fallen animal: the rule of Exodus 23:5 applied to a neighbor
decisions.reason: Exodus 23:5 tells Israel to help even an enemy whose donkey has fallen under its load. Here the same help is owed to a fellow Israelite. The animal has collapsed, probably under a load, and needs more than one person to raise it.

decisions.choice: raise them up with him: work together with the owner
decisions.reason: The words "with him" mean the passer-by is to join the owner in the work, not leave him to struggle alone. The doubled verb makes it emphatic.

decisions.choice: get it back on its feet / get the animal up again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what raising the animal means; Literal supplies "them" in brackets for the animals. Readable says "the owner" for "him".

records.source: לֹא־יִהְיֶ֤ה כְלִי־גֶ֨בֶר֙ עַל־אִשָּׁ֔ה וְלֹא־יִלְבַּ֥שׁ גֶּ֖בֶר שִׂמְלַ֣ת אִשָּׁ֑ה כִּ֧י תוֹעֲבַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ כָּל־עֹ֥שֵׂה אֵֽלֶּה׃פ
records.gloss: Not shall be [the] article of a man on a woman, and not shall put on a man [the] garment of a woman, for [the] abomination of Yahweh your God [is] every one doing these.
pieces: A woman must not wear a man's things, and a man must not put on a woman's clothing, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God detests anyone who does these things.

L.5: A man's article shall not be on a woman, and a man shall not put on a woman's garment, for everyone who does these [things is] an abomination to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God.

R.5: A woman must not wear what belongs to a man, and a man must not wear women's clothes. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God hates it when anyone does these things.

decisions.choice: the article of a man: anything that belongs to a man, not only clothing
decisions.reason: The word for the man's side is broad: an object, gear, a tool or a weapon. For the woman's side the verse uses the ordinary word for a garment. The rule covers both what is worn and what is carried.

decisions.choice: an abomination to the LORD: the outward difference between men and women is to be kept
decisions.reason: The verse gives no reason beyond calling the practice detestable to the LORD. It keeps visible the distinction between man and woman made at creation (Genesis 1:27). Some connect it with pagan rites in which men and women exchanged dress; the text does not say this.

decisions.choice: abomination: something the LORD finds detestable
decisions.reason: As in 17:1, the word names what is deeply offensive to God and rejected by him.

decisions.choice: a man's things / what belongs to a man
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the broad sense of the word rather than narrowing it to clothing. Readable says the LORD "hates it when anyone does" these things, for the Hebrew "an abomination ... is everyone doing these".

records.source: כִּ֣י יִקָּרֵ֣א קַן־צִפּ֣וֹר׀לְפָנֶ֡יךָ בַּדֶּ֜רֶךְ בְּכָל־עֵ֣ץ׀א֣וֹ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶפְרֹחִים֙ א֣וֹ בֵיצִ֔ים וְהָאֵ֤ם רֹבֶ֨צֶת֙ עַל־הָֽאֶפְרֹחִ֔ים א֖וֹ עַל־הַבֵּיצִ֑ים לֹא־תִקַּ֥ח הָאֵ֖ם עַל־הַבָּנִֽים׃
records.gloss: If is met a nest of a bird before you on the way, in any tree or on the ground, young ones or eggs, and the mother [is] sitting on the young ones or on the eggs, not you shall take the mother with the young.
pieces: If you happen to come across a bird's nest beside the road, in a tree or on the ground, with chicks or eggs in it and the mother bird sitting on the chicks or the eggs, do not take the mother along with her young.

L.6: If a bird's nest happens to be before you on the way, in any tree or on the ground, [with] young ones or eggs, and the mother [is] sitting on the young ones or on the eggs, you shall not take the mother with the young.

R.6: You may find a bird's nest by the road, in a tree or on the ground. It may have baby birds or eggs in it, with the mother bird sitting on them. Do not take the mother bird together with her babies.

decisions.choice: is met before you: comes across your path by chance
decisions.reason: The verb describes something you happen upon. The law is about a nest found while traveling, not about hunting birds.

decisions.choice: taking the young: eggs and young birds were food
decisions.reason: Wild eggs and young birds were gathered to eat. The law allows this (verse 7) but forbids taking the mother as well.

decisions.choice: the mother with the young: a phrase used for total destruction
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the mother on the sons". The same words describe the killing of whole families, mothers together with children (Genesis 32:12; Hosea 10:14). The law forbids doing to a family of birds what is the very picture of ruthless destruction.

decisions.choice: chicks / baby birds; her young / her babies
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one word for young birds and then "sons" for the same young. Balanced and Readable use everyday words; Literal keeps "young ones" and "the young".

records.heading: A bird’s nest by the road

records.source: שַׁלֵּ֤חַ תְּשַׁלַּח֙ אֶת־הָאֵ֔ם וְאֶת־הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּֽקַּֽח־לָ֑ךְ לְמַ֨עַן֙ יִ֣יטַב לָ֔ךְ וְהַאֲרַכְתָּ֖ יָמִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: Surely you shall let go the mother, and the young you may take for yourself, so that it may go well for you and you prolong days.
pieces: Be sure to let the mother go free, though you may take the young for yourself, so that things may go well with you and you may live a long life.

L.7: You shall surely let the mother go, and the young you may take for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may prolong [your] days.

R.7: You must let the mother bird go. You may take the babies for yourself. Do this so that things will go well with you and you will live a long time.

decisions.choice: so that it may go well with you and you may prolong your days: the promise of the fifth commandment
decisions.reason: The same promise is attached to honoring father and mother (5:16) and to keeping the commandments as a whole (4:40; 6:2-3). A small kindness to a bird is given the same promise as one of the Ten Commandments.

decisions.choice: let the mother go: spare the source of new life
decisions.reason: The law gives no reason, but sparing the mother lets her breed again, so the use of a gift does not destroy the giver. Other laws show the same care for living things: fruit trees in a siege (20:19), the ox treading grain (25:4), and a mother animal and her young not killed on one day (Leviticus 22:28).

decisions.choice: you may take: permission, not command
decisions.reason: The verb form can be a command or a permission. Here it allows taking the young; what is commanded is releasing the mother.

decisions.choice: live a long life / live a long time
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "prolong days" means to live long. Balanced and Readable say so; Literal keeps the idiom with "your" supplied.

records.source: כִּ֤י תִבְנֶה֙ בַּ֣יִת חָדָ֔שׁ וְעָשִׂ֥יתָ מַעֲקֶ֖ה לְגַגֶּ֑ךָ וְלֹֽא־תָשִׂ֤ים דָּמִים֙ בְּבֵיתֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי־יִפֹּ֥ל הַנֹּפֵ֖ל מִמֶּֽנּוּ׃ס
records.gloss: When you build a house new, then you shall make a parapet for your roof, and not you shall put blood on your house if falls the falling [one] from it.
pieces: When you build a new house, put a low wall around the edge of the roof, so that you do not bring guilt for a death on your household if someone falls from it.

L.8: When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, and you shall not put blood on your house if anyone falling falls from it.

R.8: When you build a new house, build a low wall around the edge of the flat roof. Then if someone falls off, you will not be guilty of that person's death.

decisions.choice: a parapet for your roof: a low wall around a flat roof
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs reached by stairs or a ladder, used for drying crops, sleeping in hot weather and spending time in the open air (Joshua 2:6; 1 Samuel 9:25-26; 2 Samuel 11:2). Without a railing wall, people could fall to their death.

decisions.choice: put blood on your house: bring guilt for someone's death on your household
decisions.reason: "Blood" (here plural, "bloods") means guilt for a death. The builder who failed to take reasonable care would bear responsibility for the life lost, as 19:10 speaks of bloodguilt coming on the people.

decisions.choice: the one falling falls: anyone who might fall
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb, "the faller falls": whoever it may be, family member or guest.

decisions.choice: a low wall around the edge of the roof
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "parapet". Balanced and Readable describe it; Readable adds "flat" to explain why a roof needs a wall. Balanced says "guilt for a death" for "blood".

records.source: לֹא־תִזְרַ֥ע כַּרְמְךָ֖ כִּלְאָ֑יִם פֶּן־תִּקְדַּ֗שׁ הַֽמְלֵאָ֤ה הַזֶּ֨רַע֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּזְרָ֔ע וּתְבוּאַ֖ת הַכָּֽרֶם׃ס
records.gloss: Not you shall sow your vineyard [with] two kinds, lest becomes holy the full [yield], the seed which you sow and [the] produce of the vineyard.
pieces: Do not sow your vineyard with a second kind of seed, or the whole yield will be forfeited to the sanctuary, both the crop you have sown and the fruit of the vineyard.

L.9: You shall not sow your vineyard [with] two kinds, lest the whole yield become holy, the seed that you sow and the produce of the vineyard.

R.9: Do not plant any other crop among the vines in your vineyard. If you do, you will lose all of it to the holy place, both what you planted and the grapes.

decisions.choice: two kinds: the law against mixing, as in Leviticus 19:19
decisions.reason: The word means "two kinds" or "a mixture". Leviticus 19:19 forbids mixing kinds of seed in a field, breeding different kinds of animal, and wearing mixed cloth. Verses 9-11 here give three such rules: seed, plowing animals and cloth.

decisions.choice: become holy: be forfeited to the sanctuary
decisions.reason: Something that becomes holy passes out of ordinary use into God's possession. The whole harvest would be lost to the owner and belong to the sanctuary. The same consonants could also be read "lest you forfeit"; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the full yield ... the produce of the vineyard: everything that grows there
decisions.reason: The first word means the full harvest. It is spelled out as both the second crop that was sown and the grapes of the vines themselves.

decisions.choice: forfeited to the sanctuary / lose all of it to the holy place
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "become holy". Balanced and Readable say what that means in practice for the owner. Readable describes the mixed sowing as planting another crop among the vines.

records.heading: Two kinds together

records.source: לֹֽא־תַחֲרֹ֥שׁ בְּשׁוֹר־וּבַחֲמֹ֖ר יַחְדָּֽו׃ס
records.gloss: Not you shall plow with an ox and with a donkey together.
pieces: Do not plow with an ox and a donkey yoked together.

L.10: You shall not plow with an ox and with a donkey together.

R.10: Do not hitch an ox and a donkey together to pull a plow.

decisions.choice: an ox and a donkey together: two animals of unlike kind under one yoke
decisions.reason: The two differ in size, strength and pace, so yoking them together would be hard on both. The ox was also a clean animal and the donkey unclean (14:4-8), and the rule stands with the laws against mixing in verses 9 and 11. The text does not say which reason is meant.

decisions.choice: yoked together: a picture used again in the New Testament
decisions.reason: Paul's warning against being "unequally yoked" (2 Corinthians 6:14) draws on this kind of law.

decisions.choice: yoked / hitch
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "together". Balanced and Readable add that the animals would be yoked or hitched side by side, which is how plowing was done.

records.source: לֹ֤א תִלְבַּשׁ֙ שַֽׁעַטְנֵ֔ז צֶ֥מֶר וּפִשְׁתִּ֖ים יַחְדָּֽו׃ס
records.gloss: Not you shall wear mixed [cloth], wool and linen together.
pieces: Do not wear clothing woven of wool and linen together.

L.11: You shall not wear mixed cloth, wool and linen together.

R.11: Do not wear clothes made from wool and linen mixed together.

decisions.choice: mixed cloth: a rare word, explained by the words that follow
decisions.reason: The word (sha'atnez) appears only here and in Leviticus 19:19. Its origin is uncertain, perhaps from another language. This verse explains it as wool and linen together, one from an animal and one from a plant.

decisions.choice: wool and linen: a mixture used in the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The tabernacle curtains and the high priest's garments combined dyed wool yarn with fine linen (Exodus 26:1; 28:6; 39:29). The rule may keep for holy use a mixture that belonged to the sanctuary, though the text gives no reason.

decisions.choice: woven of / made from
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say the cloth is made of the two fibers together; Literal says "mixed cloth".

records.source: גְּדִלִ֖ים תַּעֲשֶׂה־לָּ֑ךְ עַל־אַרְבַּ֛ע כַּנְפ֥וֹת כְּסוּתְךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תְּכַסֶּה־בָּֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: Tassels you shall make for yourself on [the] four corners of your covering with which you cover yourself.
pieces: Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wrap yourself in.

L.12: You shall make tassels for yourself on the four corners of your covering with which you cover yourself.

R.12: Put tassels on the four corners of the outer robe you wear.

decisions.choice: tassels: twisted cords on the corners of the cloak, as in Numbers 15:37-41
decisions.reason: The word here means twisted threads. Numbers 15:37-41 uses a different word for the same tassels and says what they are for: with a cord of blue in each, they remind Israel to remember and do all the LORD's commands.

decisions.choice: your covering: the outer garment, a large cloth with four corners
decisions.reason: The outer cloak was a large piece of cloth wrapped around the body, which also served as a blanket at night (Exodus 22:26). Its four corners carried the tassels.

decisions.choice: cloak / outer robe
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "covering" and the repeated "cover yourself". Balanced says "cloak", Readable "outer robe", to name the garment meant.

records.source: כִּֽי־יִקַּ֥ח אִ֖ישׁ אִשָּׁ֑ה וּבָ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ וּשְׂנֵאָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: If takes a man a woman and goes in to her and hates her,
pieces: If a man marries a woman and sleeps with her, but then turns against her,

L.13: If a man takes a wife and goes in to her, and [then] hates her,

R.13: A man may marry a woman and sleep with her, and then decide he does not like her.

decisions.choice: takes a woman and goes in to her: marries her and has intercourse with her
decisions.reason: "Take a woman" is the usual way of saying "marry" (21:13; 24:1), and "go in to her" means to have sexual intercourse, here the first night of the marriage (Genesis 29:23).

decisions.choice: hates her: rejects her, turns against her
decisions.reason: In laws about marriage "hate" means to reject or no longer want a wife, not only a feeling (21:15; 24:3). Here it explains why the man brings his charge: he wants to be rid of her.

decisions.choice: if: one case in two outcomes, verses 13-21
decisions.reason: Verses 13-17 set out the case, a husband who claims his bride was not a virgin. Verses 18-19 give the verdict if the charge is false, verses 20-21 if it is true.

decisions.choice: the setting: marriages arranged between families
decisions.reason: In ancient Israel a marriage was agreed between the families, and the bride's father received a bride-price (verse 29; Exodus 22:15-16). A bride was expected to come to marriage a virgin, and a charge that she had not touched the honor of her whole family. The laws of verses 13-29 regulate that society; they deal with a husband's charge, adultery, and sex with a woman engaged or unengaged.

decisions.choice: sleeps with her
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "goes in to her" is a plain idiom in its own language for intercourse. Balanced and Readable say "sleeps with her", the ordinary English way to say the same, without adding or softening anything. Literal keeps "goes in to her".

records.heading: Charges against a bride

records.source: וְשָׂ֥ם לָהּ֙ עֲלִילֹ֣ת דְּבָרִ֔ים וְהוֹצִ֥יא עָלֶ֖יהָ שֵׁ֣ם רָ֑ע וְאָמַ֗ר אֶת־הָאִשָּׁ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ לָקַ֔חְתִּי וָאֶקְרַ֣ב אֵלֶ֔יהָ וְלֹא־מָצָ֥אתִי לָ֖הּ בְּתוּלִֽים׃
records.gloss: and lays against her deeds of words and brings out on her a bad name, and says, This woman I took, and I came near to her, and not I found in her virginity,
pieces: and charges her with shameful behavior and ruins her reputation, saying, 'This is the woman I married, but when I slept with her, I did not find evidence that she was a virgin,'

L.14: and lays charges of shameful deeds against her and brings a bad name on her, saying, 'I took this woman, and when I came near to her, I did not find [the evidence of] virginity in her,'

R.14: So he accuses her of shameful things and spoils her good name. He says, 'I married this woman, but when I slept with her, I did not find any sign that she was a virgin.'

decisions.choice: deeds of words: charges of shameful conduct
decisions.reason: The phrase joins a word for deeds, often wanton or wicked deeds, with "words". It means accusations about her behavior. Because the man acts out of dislike (verse 13), some take it as "pretexts", charges made up as an excuse; the law still allows that they may be true (verse 20).

decisions.choice: brings out a bad name on her: publicly defames her
decisions.reason: To "bring out a bad name" is to spread a damaging report so that it becomes public (verse 19). The charge is not made in private but before the town.

decisions.choice: I came near to her: I had intercourse with her
decisions.reason: "Come near" to a woman is a Hebrew way of speaking of sexual relations (Genesis 20:4; Leviticus 18:6, 14, 19; Isaiah 8:3).

decisions.choice: virginity: here the signs that she was a virgin
decisions.reason: The word is an abstract noun, "virginity". In verses 14-20 it means the physical evidence of it, which the parents can bring out and show (verses 15, 17).

decisions.choice: [the evidence of] virginity / evidence that she was a virgin / any sign that she was a virgin
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "the evidence of" to show that the Hebrew has the single word "virginity"; Balanced and Readable say it plainly. Balanced and Readable say "slept with her" for "came near to her", as in verse 13.

records.source: וְלָקַ֛ח אֲבִ֥י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה וְאִמָּ֑הּ וְהוֹצִ֜יאוּ אֶת־בְּתוּלֵ֧י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֛ה אֶל־זִקְנֵ֥י הָעִ֖יר הַשָּֽׁעְרָה׃
records.gloss: then shall take [the] father of the young woman and her mother and bring out [the] virginity of the young woman to [the] elders of the city at the gate.
pieces: the young woman's father and mother are to take the evidence of her virginity and bring it to the elders of the town at the gate.

L.15: then the father of the young woman and her mother shall take and bring out the [evidence of the] virginity of the young woman to the elders of the city at the gate.

R.15: Then the young woman's father and mother must take the proof that she was a virgin. They must bring it to the elders of the town at the town gate.

decisions.choice: young woman: written without its last letter
decisions.reason: In the five books of Moses the word for young woman (na'arah) is usually written without its final letter, so that it looks like the word for young man (na'ar). It is read as feminine, as the context requires, here and through verse 29. The meaning is not affected.

decisions.choice: the evidence of virginity: the cloth from the wedding night
decisions.reason: Verse 17 shows that it is a cloth or garment that can be spread out. It was probably the bedding or garment from the wedding night, marked with blood when the marriage was first consummated, which the bride's family kept. Some think instead of a cloth showing that she had had her period before the wedding, so that she was not already pregnant. Either way the parents hold proof against the husband's charge.

decisions.choice: the elders of the city at the gate: the town's court
decisions.reason: The town elders sat at the gate to hear cases (21:19; Ruth 4:1-2), as in 17:5.

decisions.choice: her father and her mother: the family defends the daughter
decisions.reason: Both parents act together. The charge was an attack on their household as well as on her, and they answer it in public.

decisions.choice: evidence / proof
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the evidence as the thing brought out; Literal keeps "virginity" with "evidence of" in brackets.

records.source: וְאָמַ֛ר אֲבִ֥י הַֽנַּעַרָ֖האֶל־הַזְּקֵנִ֑ים אֶת־בִּתִּ֗י נָתַ֜תִּי לָאִ֥ישׁ הַזֶּ֛ה לְאִשָּׁ֖ה וַיִּשְׂנָאֶֽהָ׃
records.gloss: And shall say [the] father of the young woman to the elders, My daughter I gave to the man the this as wife, and he hates her;
pieces: The young woman's father is to say to the elders, 'I gave my daughter to this man in marriage, but he has turned against her.

L.16: And the father of the young woman shall say to the elders, 'I gave my daughter to this man as wife, and he hates her;

R.16: Her father must say to the elders, 'I gave my daughter to this man to be his wife. But now he does not like her.

decisions.choice: I gave my daughter as wife: the father gave her in marriage
decisions.reason: A daughter's marriage was arranged by her father, who received the bride-price (verse 29). So the father speaks for the family before the court.

decisions.choice: he hates her: he has rejected her
decisions.reason: As in verse 13: the father names the motive behind the charge.

decisions.choice: in marriage
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "as wife". Balanced says "gave ... in marriage", the usual English for a father's part in a wedding.

records.source: וְהִנֵּה־ה֡וּא שָׂם֩ עֲלִילֹ֨ת דְּבָרִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר לֹֽא־מָצָ֤אתִי לְבִתְּךָ֙ בְּתוּלִ֔ים וְאֵ֖לֶּה בְּתוּלֵ֣י בִתִּ֑י וּפָֽרְשׂוּ֙ הַשִּׂמְלָ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י זִקְנֵ֥י הָעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And look, he has laid deeds of words, saying, Not I found in your daughter virginity; and these [are the] virginity of my daughter. And they shall spread the garment before [the] elders of the city.
pieces: Now he has charged her with shameful behavior, saying, "I did not find evidence that your daughter was a virgin." But here is the evidence of my daughter's virginity.' Then they are to spread out the cloth in front of the elders of the town.

L.17: and look, he has laid charges of shameful deeds, saying, "I did not find [the evidence of] virginity in your daughter." But these [are the evidence of] my daughter's virginity.' And they shall spread the garment before the elders of the city.

R.17: He has accused her of shameful things. He says, "I did not find any sign that your daughter was a virgin." But here is the proof that my daughter was a virgin.' Then the parents must spread out the cloth for the elders of the town to see.

decisions.choice: and look: the father points to what the husband has done
decisions.reason: The little word that usually means "look" draws attention to the charge as a fact before the court, and then to the proof set against it.

decisions.choice: the garment: the cloth that holds the evidence
decisions.reason: The word is the same as the cloak of verse 3, a large cloth or garment. Spread out before the elders, it shows the signs of the wedding night (see verse 15).

decisions.choice: they: the young woman's parents
decisions.reason: The plural verb refers to the father and mother of verse 15.

decisions.choice: nested quotation marks
decisions.reason: The father's words are a quotation inside Moses' speech, so they take single quotation marks; the husband's words that the father repeats inside them take double marks.

decisions.choice: the parents ... for the elders of the town to see
decisions.reason: Readable names who spreads the cloth and why, from verse 15 and the phrase "before the elders".

records.source: וְלָֽקְח֛וּ זִקְנֵ֥י הָֽעִיר־הַהִ֖וא אֶת־הָאִ֑ישׁ וְיִסְּר֖וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And shall take [the] elders of the city the that the man and shall discipline him,
pieces: The elders of that town are then to take the man and punish him,

L.18: And the elders of that city shall take the man and discipline him,

R.18: Then the elders of that town must take the man and punish him.

decisions.choice: discipline him: punish him, most likely by flogging
alternatives: punish him by the fine that follows
decisions.reason: The verb means to correct or discipline, and can mean to punish by beating (1 Kings 12:11). It probably means a flogging such as 25:1-3 describes. It could also refer to the fine of verse 19 as the way he is punished.

decisions.choice: the verdict if the charge is false
decisions.reason: The verse does not say "if the charge is false"; the evidence shown in verse 17 has already proved it. The sentence runs on into verse 19.

decisions.choice: punish
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "punish", which covers what the verb means here without deciding the form of the punishment; Literal keeps "discipline".

records.source: וְעָנְשׁ֨וּ אֹת֜וֹ מֵ֣אָה כֶ֗סֶף וְנָתְנוּ֙ לַאֲבִ֣י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה כִּ֤י הוֹצִיא֙ שֵׁ֣ם רָ֔ע עַ֖ל בְּתוּלַ֣ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֽוֹ־תִהְיֶ֣ה לְאִשָּׁ֔ה לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל לְשַּׁלְּחָ֖הּכָּל־יָמָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: and they shall fine him a hundred [of] silver and give [it] to [the] father of the young woman, because he brought out a bad name on a virgin of Israel; and to him she shall be for a wife; not he is able to send her away all his days.
pieces: and fine him {{units:about 2 1/2 pounds of silver|a hundred shekels of silver}}, which they are to give to the young woman's father, because this man has ruined the reputation of a virgin of Israel. She is to remain his wife, and he may never divorce her as long as he lives.

L.19: and they shall fine him a hundred [shekels of] silver and give [them] to the father of the young woman, because he brought out a bad name on a virgin of Israel. And she shall be his wife; he may not send her away all his days.

R.19: They must also make him pay {{units:about 2 1/2 pounds of silver|a hundred shekels of silver}} to the young woman's father. This is because he has spoiled the good name of a young woman of Israel who was a virgin. She will stay his wife, and he may never divorce her as long as he lives.

decisions.choice: a hundred of silver: a hundred shekels, twice the bride-price
decisions.reason: The weight is understood to be shekels, as in verse 29. A hundred shekels is double the fifty paid for a virgin in verse 29 (Exodus 22:16). It is paid to the father, whose family he has shamed. The penalty is not the one he tried to bring on her; compare 19:19, where a false witness suffers what he planned for another.

decisions.choice: a virgin of Israel: the slander is a wrong against the people
decisions.reason: By calling her "a virgin of Israel" the law treats the false charge as an offense not only against one woman and her family but against Israel, just as her guilt in verse 21 would be "a disgraceful thing in Israel".

decisions.choice: he may not send her away all his days: he loses the right to divorce her
decisions.reason: "Send away" is the word for divorce (24:1-4). The man wanted to be rid of her; the law takes away that right for life, so that she cannot be cast off and left without a home or support. The law does not say whether she could leave the marriage.

decisions.choice: about 2 1/2 pounds of silver
decisions.reason: A shekel weighed about two-fifths of an ounce, so a hundred shekels is about 40 ounces. Balanced and Readable give the modern weight with the original as the alternative; Literal keeps the Hebrew "a hundred of silver" with "shekels" in brackets.

records.source: וְאִם־אֱמֶ֣ת הָיָ֔ה הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה לֹא־נִמְצְא֥וּ בְתוּלִ֖ים לַֽנַּעֲרָֽה׃
records.gloss: But if truth was the word the this, not were found virginity for the young woman,
pieces: But if the charge is true, and no evidence of the young woman's virginity is found,

L.20: But if this thing was true, [and evidence of] virginity was not found for the young woman,

R.20: But the charge may be true, and there may be no proof that the young woman was a virgin.

decisions.choice: but if: the other outcome of the case
decisions.reason: The law now turns to the case where the husband's charge holds: the parents cannot bring the evidence of verse 15.

decisions.choice: this word: this charge
decisions.reason: "Word" here is the matter or accusation the husband has made.

decisions.choice: [and evidence of]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words needed to show that the Hebrew has the one word "virginity", as in verse 14.

records.source: וְהוֹצִ֨יאוּ אֶת־הַֽנַּעֲרָ֜ה אֶל־פֶּ֣תַח בֵּית־אָבִ֗יהָ וּסְקָלוּהָ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י עִירָ֤הּ בָּאֲבָנִים֙ וָמֵ֔תָה כִּֽי־עָשְׂתָ֤ה נְבָלָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִזְנ֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑יהָ וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃ס
records.gloss: then they shall bring out the young woman to [the] entrance of [the] house of her father, and shall stone her [the] men of her city with stones, and she shall die, because she has done a disgraceful folly in Israel, to act as a prostitute [in the] house of her father; and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
pieces: then they are to bring her out to the doorway of her father's house, and there the men of her town are to stone her to death, because she has done an outrageous thing in Israel by being sexually immoral while living in her father's house. In this way you will remove the evil from among you.

L.21: then they shall bring the young woman out to the entrance of her father's house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones, and she shall die, because she has done a disgraceful thing in Israel by prostituting herself [in] her father's house. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.

R.21: Then they must bring her out to the door of her father's house. There the men of her town must kill her by throwing stones at her. She has done a shameful thing in Israel. She was sexually immoral while she was still living in her father's house. This is how you must get rid of the evil among you.

decisions.choice: disgraceful folly: a gross wrong that disgraces the community
decisions.reason: The word names an outrageous act, often a sexual wrong, that brings shame on the whole people (Genesis 34:7; Judges 20:6, 10; 2 Samuel 13:12). The words "in Israel" say that the shame falls on the people of the covenant.

decisions.choice: to act as a prostitute: to have sexual relations outside marriage
decisions.reason: The verb is used of prostitution, but also more widely of any sexual relations outside marriage (Genesis 38:24). Here it means that she had intercourse while still under her father's roof and then entered the marriage as though she were a virgin.

decisions.choice: the entrance of her father's house: the place where the wrong was done
decisions.reason: Executions were normally outside the town gate (verse 24; 17:5). This one is at the door of her father's house, where the wrong took place and whose head was responsible for her.

decisions.choice: remove the evil from your midst: get rid of the evil completely
decisions.reason: The refrain of Deuteronomy's laws, as in 17:7. It returns in verses 22 and 24.

decisions.choice: being sexually immoral
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "prostituting herself", the verb's basic sense. Balanced and Readable say "sexually immoral", the sense here (see the meaning decision), since no payment is in view.

records.source: כִּֽי־יִמָּצֵ֨א אִ֜ישׁ שֹׁכֵ֣ב׀עִם־אִשָּׁ֣ה בְעֻֽלַת־בַּ֗עַל וּמֵ֨תוּ֙ גַּם־שְׁנֵיהֶ֔ם הָאִ֛ישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵ֥ב עִם־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וְהָאִשָּׁ֑ה וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: If is found a man lying with a woman married to a husband, then they shall die also both of them, the man lying with the woman, and the woman; and you shall remove the evil from Israel.
pieces: If a man is caught sleeping with another man's wife, both of them must die, the man who slept with her and the woman as well. In this way you will remove the evil from Israel.

L.22: If a man is found lying with a woman married to a husband, then both of them shall die, the man who lay with the woman, and the woman. So you shall remove the evil from Israel.

R.22: A man may be caught sleeping with another man's wife. Then both of them must be put to death, the man and the woman. This is how you must get rid of the evil in Israel.

decisions.choice: a woman married to a husband: a married woman
decisions.reason: The phrase is literally "a woman possessed by a husband"; the word for husband also means master or owner. It is the legal way of naming a married woman (Genesis 20:3).

decisions.choice: they shall die: the law of adultery
decisions.reason: The commandment forbids adultery (5:18), and Leviticus 20:10 sets the same penalty for both the man and the woman.

decisions.choice: is found: caught in the act
decisions.reason: "Found" means discovered while it happens or proved by witnesses; the rule of two or three witnesses stands for every capital case (17:6; 19:15).

decisions.choice: also both of them: the penalty is the same for each
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses "both of them" and then names each, the man and the woman, so that neither is spared at the other's expense.

decisions.choice: sleeping with another man's wife
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "lying with a woman married to a husband". Balanced and Readable say "sleeping with" for the Hebrew "lying with", as in verse 13, and "another man's wife" for the legal phrase.

records.heading: A married or engaged woman

records.source: כִּ֤י יִהְיֶה֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה בְתוּלָ֔ה מְאֹרָשָׂ֖ה לְאִ֑ישׁ וּמְצָאָ֥הּ אִ֛ישׁ בָּעִ֖יר וְשָׁכַ֥ב עִמָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: If there is a young woman, a virgin, betrothed to a man, and finds her a man in [the] city and lies with her,
pieces: If a young woman who is a virgin is engaged to a man, and another man meets her in the town and sleeps with her,

L.23: If there is a young woman, a virgin, betrothed to a man, and a man finds her in the city and lies with her,

R.23: Suppose a young woman who is a virgin is engaged to be married. Then another man meets her in the town and sleeps with her.

decisions.choice: betrothed: bound by a marriage agreement, though not yet living with her husband
decisions.reason: Betrothal was a binding stage of marriage. The bride-price had been agreed or paid, and the woman was counted as the man's wife (verse 24 calls her "his neighbor's wife"), though the wedding had not taken place (20:7; Matthew 1:18-19). Sex with her was therefore treated like adultery.

decisions.choice: finds her: comes upon her
decisions.reason: The verb itself says nothing about force or consent. In this case and the next, the place where it happens decides the matter (verses 24, 27).

decisions.choice: young woman: written without its last letter
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

decisions.choice: engaged
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "betrothed". Balanced and Readable say "engaged", the modern word nearest to it; the meaning decision explains that betrothal was more binding than an engagement today. They say "another man" to make clear the second man is not her betrothed.

records.source: וְהוֹצֵאתֶ֨ם אֶת־שְׁנֵיהֶ֜ם אֶל־שַׁ֣עַר׀הָעִ֣יר הַהִ֗וא וּסְקַלְתֶּ֨ם אֹתָ֥ם בָּאֲבָנִים֮ וָמֵתוּ֒ אֶת־הַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ה עַל־דְּבַר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־צָעֲקָ֣ה בָעִ֔יר וְאֶ֨ת־הָאִ֔ישׁ עַל־דְּבַ֥ר אֲשֶׁר־עִנָּ֖ה אֶת־אֵ֣שֶׁת רֵעֵ֑הוּ וּבִֽעַרְתָּ֥ הָרָ֖ע מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃ס
records.gloss: then you shall bring out both of them to [the] gate of the city the that and stone them with stones and they shall die: the young woman because that not she cried out in [the] city, and the man because that he humbled [the] wife of his neighbor; and you shall remove the evil from your midst.
pieces: you are to take both of them out to the gate of that town and stone them to death: the young woman because, though she was in the town, she did not cry for help, and the man because he dishonored another man's wife. In this way you will remove the evil from among you.

L.24: then you shall bring both of them out to the gate of that city and stone them with stones, and they shall die: the young woman because she did not cry out in the city, and the man because he humbled his neighbor's wife. So you shall remove the evil from your midst.

R.24: Take them both out to the gate of that town and kill them by throwing stones. The young woman must die because she did not shout for help, even though she was in the town where people could hear. The man must die because he dishonored another man's wife. This is how you must get rid of the evil among you.

decisions.choice: she did not cry out in the city: in a town, a cry for help would be heard
decisions.reason: The law judges by the place. In a town, people were near enough to hear and come; if she did not call for help, the law takes it that she consented. It is a rule of evidence for a case with no other witnesses, set against the case in the countryside (verses 25-27).

decisions.choice: humbled: dishonored, took her honor by sexual relations
decisions.reason: The verb means to humble, degrade or violate. It is used of rape (Genesis 34:2; 2 Samuel 13:12, 14) and here of sex with a woman pledged to another. It names the wrong done to her and to the man she is to marry, whether or not she consented.

decisions.choice: the wife of his neighbor: a betrothed woman is counted as a wife
decisions.reason: She is called a wife though the marriage has not begun (verse 23), which is why the penalty is that of adultery (verse 22).

decisions.choice: dishonored
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "humbled". Balanced and Readable say "dishonored", which keeps the sense of degrading without saying that force was used, since here the law takes it that she consented. In verse 29 Balanced says "violated" for the same verb, where the man seized her.

decisions.choice: where people could hear
decisions.reason: Readable adds the reason the place matters, from the contrast with verse 27.

records.source: וְֽאִם־בַּשָּׂדֶ֞ה יִמְצָ֣א הָאִ֗ישׁ אֶת־הַֽנַּעֲרָה֙ הַמְאֹ֣רָשָׂ֔ה וְהֶחֱזִֽיק־בָּ֥הּ הָאִ֖ישׁ וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ וּמֵ֗ת הָאִ֛ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־שָׁכַ֥ב עִמָּ֖הּ לְבַדּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: But if in the field finds the man the young woman the betrothed, and seizes her the man and lies with her, then shall die the man who lay with her, him alone.
pieces: But if the man comes upon the engaged young woman out in the countryside, and he overpowers her and rapes her, then only the man who did this must die.

L.25: But if the man finds the betrothed young woman in the field, and the man seizes her and lies with her, then only the man who lay with her shall die.

R.25: But suppose the man meets the engaged young woman out in the open country. He grabs her and rapes her. Then only the man must be put to death.

decisions.choice: seizes her: takes hold of her by force
decisions.reason: The verb means to grasp firmly or overpower (Judges 19:25; 2 Samuel 13:11, 14). With "lies with her" it describes rape. Verse 23 has no word of force; this verse does.

decisions.choice: in the field: open country, away from any town
decisions.reason: "The field" is the open land outside a town, where no one might be near to hear or help (verse 27).

decisions.choice: him alone: only the man is guilty
decisions.reason: The words put the whole guilt on the man. Verse 26 says why the young woman bears none.

decisions.choice: overpowers her and rapes her
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "seizes her and lies with her". Together the two verbs describe rape, and Balanced and Readable say so plainly. Literal keeps the two verbs. Balanced and Readable shorten "the man who lay with her" to "the man who did this" and "the man".

records.source: וְלַֽנַּעֲרָה֙לֹא־תַעֲשֶׂ֣ה דָבָ֔ר אֵ֥ין לַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה חֵ֣טְא מָ֑וֶת כִּ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יָק֨וּם אִ֤ישׁ עַל־רֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ וּרְצָח֣וֹ נֶ֔פֶשׁ כֵּ֖ן הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: But to the young woman not you shall do anything; there is not for the young woman a sin of death, for as when rises a man against his neighbor and murders him, [a] life, so [is] the matter the this.
pieces: Do nothing to the young woman; she has committed no sin that deserves death. This case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and murders him.

L.26: But to the young woman you shall do nothing; there is in the young woman no sin [worthy] of death, for as when a man rises against his neighbor and murders him, [taking his] life, so [is] this case.

R.26: Do not do anything to the young woman. She has done nothing wrong that deserves death. What happened to her is like a man attacking his neighbor and murdering him.

decisions.choice: a sin of death: a sin that carries the death penalty
decisions.reason: The phrase means guilt that deserves death (compare 21:22). The young woman has no such guilt.

decisions.choice: as when a man rises against his neighbor: she is the victim of a violent crime
decisions.reason: The law compares the case to murder. The one attacked is not to blame for the attack, and the woman is no more to blame for what was done to her. The man's act is treated as violence against her, not as a shared wrong.

decisions.choice: murders him, a life: kills him outright
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds "life" (nefesh) after the verb: he strikes the person dead, taking his life. Some take it as "murders him in cold blood".

decisions.choice: This case is like ...
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "as when ... so is this case". Balanced and Readable put the comparison in one direct sentence. Literal keeps the Hebrew shape with bracketed words.

records.source: כִּ֥י בַשָּׂדֶ֖ה מְצָאָ֑הּ צָעֲקָ֗ה הַֽנַּעֲרָה֙ הַמְאֹ֣רָשָׂ֔ה וְאֵ֥ין מוֹשִׁ֖יעַ לָֽהּ׃ס
records.gloss: For in the field he found her; cried out the young woman the betrothed, and there was no one saving her.
pieces: He came upon her out in the countryside; the engaged young woman cried for help, but there was no one there to rescue her.

L.27: For he found her in the field; the betrothed young woman cried out, and there was no one to save her.

R.27: He found her out in the open country. She cried for help, but there was no one there to save her.

decisions.choice: she cried out: the law takes it that she did
decisions.reason: No witness can say what happened in the open country. The law gives the young woman the benefit of the doubt: it holds that she cried out, and that no one was near to hear.

decisions.choice: no one saving her: no one to rescue her
decisions.reason: The word is the participle of the verb "save, rescue", used of anyone who delivers someone in danger (Judges 3:9).

decisions.choice: cried for help
decisions.reason: Balanced says what her cry was; Literal keeps "cried out".

records.source: כִּֽי־יִמְצָ֣א אִ֗ישׁ נַעֲרָ֤ה בְתוּלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹא־אֹרָ֔שָׂה וּתְפָשָׂ֖הּ וְשָׁכַ֣ב עִמָּ֑הּ וְנִמְצָֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: If finds a man a young woman, a virgin who not is betrothed, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are found,
pieces: If a man comes upon a young woman who is a virgin and not engaged, and he seizes her and sleeps with her, and they are discovered,

L.28: If a man finds a young woman, a virgin who is not betrothed, and seizes her and lies with her, and they are found,

R.28: Suppose a man meets a young woman who is a virgin and is not engaged. He seizes her and sleeps with her, and people find out.

decisions.choice: seizes her: takes hold of her, probably by force
alternatives: takes her, by persuasion as in Exodus 22:15
decisions.reason: The verb means to grab or take hold of, and is used of capturing people and towns (9:17; 20:19; 21:19). It describes force, as in verse 25, though a different verb is used there. The similar law in Exodus 22:15-16 speaks of a man who persuades a girl, and some read this verse as the same case, a seduction; others read it as rape. The words "they are found" speak of both together, which some take to mean she was not forced.

decisions.choice: who is not betrothed: no other man's marriage is involved
decisions.reason: Because she is not pledged to anyone, this is not treated as adultery and carries no death penalty. The wrong is against her and her father's household, and the law settles it by payment and marriage (verse 29).

decisions.choice: they are found: the act is discovered
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 22: what happened becomes known.

decisions.choice: young woman: written without its last letter
decisions.reason: As in verse 15.

decisions.choice: seizes her and sleeps with her
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep "seizes" so that the uncertainty about force stays as open as in the Hebrew, and say "sleeps with" for "lies with", as elsewhere in this chapter.

records.source: וְ֠נָתַן הָאִ֨ישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵ֥ב עִמָּ֛הּ לַאֲבִ֥י הַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים כָּ֑סֶף וְלֽוֹ־תִהְיֶ֣ה לְאִשָּׁ֗ה תַּ֚חַת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִנָּ֔הּ לֹא־יוּכַ֥ל שַׁלְּחָ֖הכָּל־יָמָֽיו׃ס
records.gloss: then shall give the man lying with her to [the] father of the young woman fifty [of] silver, and to him she shall be for a wife, because that he humbled her; not he is able to send her away all his days.
pieces: the man who slept with her must pay the young woman's father {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds of silver|fifty shekels of silver}}, and she is to become his wife because he violated her. He may never divorce her as long as he lives.

L.29: then the man who lay with her shall give to the father of the young woman fifty [shekels of] silver, and she shall be his wife because he humbled her; he may not send her away all his days.

R.29: Then the man must pay the young woman's father {{units:about 1 1/4 pounds of silver|fifty shekels of silver}}. He must marry her, because he has dishonored her. He may never divorce her as long as he lives.

decisions.choice: fifty of silver: fifty shekels, the bride-price for a virgin
decisions.reason: Exodus 22:16 speaks of "the bride-price of virgins", and this amount was probably its standard value. It is half the fine for a false charge (verse 19). It goes to the father, who had the right to give his daughter in marriage.

decisions.choice: she shall be his wife; he may not send her away: a lifelong duty to provide for her
decisions.reason: In that society a woman who had lost her virginity outside marriage could find it hard to marry, and an unmarried woman without a household could be left without support. The law binds the man to marry her and takes away his right to divorce her, as in verse 19. Exodus 22:16 lets the father refuse the marriage; this verse does not say whether that right, or the woman's own wishes, still applied.

decisions.choice: he humbled her: he violated her
decisions.reason: The verb of verse 24. Here, with "seizes" in verse 28, it names the wrong done to her.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew chapter ends here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does, where chapter 22 has 29 verses. Many Bibles add the next verse to this chapter as 22:30, so 23:1 here is 22:30 there, and 23:2-26 here is 23:1-25 there. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: about 1 1/4 pounds of silver
decisions.reason: Fifty shekels at about two-fifths of an ounce each is about 20 ounces. Balanced and Readable give the modern weight with the original as the alternative; Literal keeps the Hebrew "fifty of silver" with "shekels" in brackets.

decisions.choice: violated / dishonored
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "humbled". Balanced says "violated", since the man took hold of her (verse 28); Readable says "dishonored", as in verse 24, a simpler word with the same sense.
